target.title: fix(collectors): harden diagnostic evidence retention
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Kova could report incomplete or misleading collector evidence when diagnostics arrived late, artifacts were still being written, files shared a basename, timeline data was partially malformed, resource sampling failed, or environment resolution failed. Some attribution totals also accepted missing or non-numeric inputs as real zeroes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps collector evidence truthful and bounded across the full collection path:

- retain collision-safe diagnostic artifacts only after they stabilize
- use one deadline-aware diagnostic session for heap and report capture
- exclude stale/pre-signal reports and bound validation memory/concurrency
- preserve malformed timeline and state-fixture failures as explicit harness evidence
- keep resource sampling failures distinct from zero resource use
- harden numeric normalization and stage-total fallbacks
- preserve current `main` process-safety and artifact-confidentiality behavior after rebase

## User Impact

Kova reports now distinguish missing, partial, stale, malformed, and failed evidence instead of silently producing optimistic metrics. Diagnostic capture is more reliable under slow writes and large artifact sets, while remaining deadline- and memory-bounded.

## Evidence

- `NO_COLOR=1 npm run check:full`
- self-check isolation: pass
- Kova self-check: 249/249 pass
- render snapshots: 21/21 pass, 0 rewritten
- web payload check: 1/1 pass
- release contract checks: pass
- structured high-reasoning branch review completed; its sole proposed finding was rejected after direct verification because `plugins.metadata.scan` is already retained by `isTurnAttributionEvent` and covered by the attribution self-check
